key_insight: Selective Backpropagation (SBP) pre-allocates which parameters can learn new classes, preserving past knowledge while keeping few-shot class-incremental learning fast and compute-efficient.
engineering_relevance: For deployment-constrained learning systems, SBP offers a practical stability-plasticity trade-off by reducing catastrophic forgetting without the replay memory or training overhead of many prior methods.
method: Restrict gradient updates to a predetermined subset of network parameters.
Freeze the remaining weights to protect previously learned knowledge.
Avoid expensive mask optimization while retaining capacity for future sessions.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmark SBP on standard FSCIL tests, cross-domain settings, and an 80-session ImageNet-1K stream, reporting strong accuracy with training time close to naive fine-tuning and lower than prior SOTA methods.
watch_item: Standard FSCIL results can overstate real-world robustness, so performance should also be checked under distribution shift and long learning horizons.
paper_title: Selective Backpropagation for Efficient Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
